related_synthesis_entries.claim: Under the source's n-to-log-t correspondence, damped or truncated logarithmic sums on both sides convert relative evaluation-point scale into the same c wedge 1 covariance, with separate proofs above and below the natural boundary scale.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The paper proves matching limits for these observables; it does not establish a universal random-matrix model for all zeta statistics.
related_synthesis_entries.title: One logarithmic covariance kernel on the matrix and zeta sides

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Both zero counts and unitary eigenvalue counts inherit Gaussian laws because a centered interval count is represented by the difference of imaginary logarithms at its endpoints, making shared endpoints control covariance.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The stated mesoscopic laws are distinct from microscopic pair-repulsion results and do not replace them.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Counting statistics are endpoint differences of log observables

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The useful correspondence is local, not just the slogan n corresponds to log t. Radial regularization of the characteristic polynomial matches the zeta abscissa shift, angular separation matches ordinate separation, and taking imaginary-log differences transfers the same Gaussian mechanism to eigenvalue counts.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For Haar unitary matrices, normalized vectors of log characteristic polynomials at radially and angularly shifted points converge to a complex Gaussian vector whose covariance is set by logarithmic relative separations; at or inside the 1/n scale the normalization changes to log n. The identity expressing a centered eigenvalue count as the difference of imaginary logarithms at its endpoints then yields Gaussian limits for consecutive interval counts.
directed.conceptual_reading: The theorem refines the matrix-zeta dictionary by matching both the large parameter and the two kinds of local displacement. It also shows that counting laws are inherited from a more primitive logarithmic observable through an endpoint operator.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The characteristic polynomial is the matrix-side bridge object, and Im log Z at two endpoints is the representation that converts its field fluctuations into eigenvalue counts. The mapping n to log t, radius to abscissa, and angle to ordinate organizes the analogy.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is an analogue with separately proved matrix mathematics, not an identification of matrices with zeta zeros. When adjacent separation exponents differ, the count covariance is more complicated than the special uniform-scale law.
directed.uncertainty: Slash, comparison, and index glyphs are imperfect in formulas (1.10)-(1.11), but the theorem's scale dictionary and endpoint identity are explicit in prose.

supported: The span explicitly states the n-to-log-t correspondence and matches radial displacement with a zeta abscissa shift and angular displacement with an ordinate shift.
The Haar-unitary log-characteristic-polynomial vector has a Gaussian limit, and the displayed imaginary-log endpoint identity yields a Gaussian limit for consecutive centered eigenvalue counts.
The candidate correctly retains the warning that unequal adjacent separation exponents lead to a more complicated covariance depending on their relative order.
inference: Calling the endpoint difference an operator that transfers fluctuations of the logarithmic observable to counts is a faithful conceptual restatement of the displayed identity.
Saying this is an analogy rather than an identification of matrices with zeta zeros is a sound scope boundary.
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase 'at or inside the 1/n scale' resolves a degraded comparison glyph and includes the equality case more precisely than this frozen span permits; the text layer securely shows only that a second epsilon_n-versus-1/n regime uses log n normalization.

context_or_ocr_risk: The comparison signs in the two epsilon_n regimes, together with slash and index glyphs in (1.10)-(1.11), are degraded. Exact regime wording must not be reconstructed without a scan.
revision_instructions: Replace 'at or inside the 1/n scale' with 'in the second epsilon_n-versus-1/n regime specified in the theorem' (or another comparison-neutral formulation), and leave the exact inequality for scan verification. related_synthesis_entries.claim: Expanding log Z in traces and approximating log zeta by prime phases reduce both vector theorems to triangular-array Gaussian limits controlled by L2 mass and tail concentration, while arithmetic additionally requires quantitative time-to-torus comparison.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The arithmetic proposition has a different cutoff condition and uses unique factorization; the analogy is structural, not identity of proofs.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Parallel CLT engines after representation change

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The branch conventions are mathematically active: they turn log Z into an L2 trace-power series and give log zeta a controlled boundary value. With those representations fixed, the matrix and zeta arguments can be compared as two Gaussian-limit problems for linear coefficient arrays rather than as opaque logarithms.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines complex Gaussian vectors through their linear combinations and covariance matrices. It defines log zeta by integrating zeta'/zeta, with a limiting convention at zero ordinates, and defines log Z outside the unit circle by the principal-branch expansion -sum_j Tr(u^j)/(jX^j), extending this definition to the circle in L2.
directed.conceptual_reading: Choosing a logarithm and its mode of boundary extension determines which linear structure is available. The trace expansion exposes the characteristic polynomial as a class-function linear statistic, preparing exactly the coefficient estimates needed by the matrix CLT.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The trace-power series is the matrix representation; the short prime expansion announced for zeta is its arithmetic counterpart. The stated bridge is methodological: Diaconis-Evans on traces parallels the later number-theoretic proposition on prime phases.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Definitions and proof architecture do not themselves establish the Gaussian limits. The boundary definition of log Z is L2 rather than pointwise, and the definition of log zeta must account for ordinates containing zeros.
directed.uncertainty: Some summation and conjugation glyphs are noisy, but the integral definition, trace expansion, L2 boundary convention, and claimed proof parallel are legible.

supported: The span defines complex Gaussian vectors via linear combinations and covariance, defines log zeta through an integral of zeta'/zeta with a limiting convention at zero ordinates, and defines log Z by a principal-branch trace series with an L2 extension to the unit circle.

It explicitly says the matrix and zeta theorems are independent but better understood by comparing similar proofs, and calls Proposition 3.1 a strict number-theoretic analogue of the Diaconis-Evans theorem.
inference: The claim that the trace series turns log Z into a class-function linear statistic is directly justified by the displayed sum of traces.
Treating branch and boundary conventions as mathematically active is reasonable because those conventions determine the displayed representations and the L2 meaning on the circle.
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase 'the short prime expansion announced for zeta' imports the mechanism of a later section: this span names Proposition 3.1 and the proof analogy but does not say that Proposition 3.1 is a short-prime expansion.

The spontaneous claim that both sides have already become 'linear coefficient arrays' overstates this span; only the matrix trace array is displayed here, while the arithmetic analogue remains unnamed beyond its proposition number.

context_or_ocr_risk: Summation, conjugation, and covariance glyphs are noisy, but the integral definition, trace expansion, L2 extension, and stated methodological comparison remain readable.
missed_mechanism: The candidate should preserve the source's deliberate distinction that the two theorems are independent even though their proofs are similar.
